title: mime-tree: base64 decode allocates stripped copy of full body even when max_bytes is None
description: decode.rs: the base64 path strips CR/LF by pushing non-newline bytes into a new Vec<u8> in a for loop (no capacity hint). For a 10 MB base64 attachment (common for PDF), this allocates a second ~10 MB Vec before passing to BASE64_STANDARD.decode() which allocates a third ~7.5 MB buffer. Total transient allocation: ~3x the body size. Fix: use Vec::with_capacity(body_bytes.len()) for the stripped buffer, or use a base64 engine that accepts a custom byte iterator to avoid the intermediate copy.
